title: How Pioneer Transcription Factors Search for Target Sites on Nucleosomal DNA.
authors: Felipe, Cayke; Shin, Jaeoh; Kolomeisky, Anatoly B
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
one_liner_zh: 该文通过离散随机模型和蒙特卡洛模拟研究先锋转录因子在核小体DNA上的靶点搜索动态，聚焦TF-DNA互作机制，方法为物理建模与模拟，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: All major biological processes start after protein molecules known as transcription factors detect specific regulatory sequences on DNA and initiate genetic expression by associating to them. But in eukaryotic cells, much of the DNA is covered by nucleosomes and other chromatin structures, preventing transcription factors from binding to their targets. At the same time, experimental studies show that there are several classes of proteins, called "pioneer transcription factors", that are able to reach the targets on nucleosomal DNA; however, the underlying microscopic mechanisms remain not well understood. We propose a new theoretical approach that might explain how pioneer transcription factors can find their targets. It is argued that pioneer transcription factors might weaken the interactions between the DNA and nucleosome by substituting them with similar interactions between transcription factors and DNA. Using this idea, we develop a discrete-state stochastic model that allows for exact calculations of target search dynamics on nucleosomal DNA using first-passage probabilities approach. It is found that the target search on nuclesomal DNA for pioneer transcription factors might be significantly accelerated while the search is slower on naked DNA in comparison with normal transcription factors. Our theoretical predictions are supported by Monte Carlo computer simulations, and they also agree with available experimental observations.
abstract_zh: 所有主要的生物过程始于被称为转录因子的蛋白质分子识别DNA上的特定调控序列，并通过与之结合启动基因表达。但在真核细胞中，大部分DNA被核小体和其他染色质结构覆盖，阻碍了转录因子与其靶标结合。同时，实验研究表明，有几类蛋白质，称为“先锋转录因子 (pioneer transcription factors)”，能够到达核小体DNA上的靶标；然而，其潜在的微观机制仍未被充分理解。我们提出了一种新的理论方法，可能解释先锋转录因子如何找到其靶标。我们论证，先锋转录因子可能通过用转录因子与DNA之间的相似相互作用替代DNA与核小体之间的相互作用，从而削弱后者。基于这一想法，我们开发了一个离散状态随机模型，利用首次通过概率方法，能够精确计算核小体DNA上的靶标搜索动力学。研究发现，与正常转录因子相比，先锋转录因子在核小体DNA上的靶标搜索可能显著加速，而在裸露DNA上的搜索则较慢。我们的理论预测得到了蒙特卡洛计算机模拟的支持，并且与现有的实验观察结果一致。
